_readme: WHY THIS EXISTS: on 2026-08-07 a reconciliation found 7 of 9 filing candidates
already fixed upstream. Every false 'still valid' had come from grepping commit
messages or trusting a stale local view. Upstream now ships daily, so a draft
hardened last week is not evidence about this week.
THE RULE THIS ENCODES: a claim is verified against SOURCE, never against commit
titles. Each item names a file and a pattern whose presence or absence decides
whether the bug still exists. If the file or anchor is missing, the verdict is
UNKNOWN -- never 'still valid'. Absence of evidence is not evidence of absence.
python3 scripts/verify_upstream.py '/path/to/vibium-source' --issues   # also check issue states via gh
Run this immediately before filing anything. Not at hardening time -- ten days
of drift was enough to kill four hardened drafts.

_why: Guards against the worst failure: running the verifier on a stale checkout and
reading its answers as current. Each landmark is a fix known to have landed on
a date; if a landmark is missing, the checkout predates it and every 'still
